_about: Organs and skeletal groups assembled from atlas structures: match rules, aliases, URL aliases and the system and region each belongs to. Enriched anatomy articles live in anatomy.json.

organs.name: Brain
organs.summary: The cerebrum, cerebellum and brainstem: about 1.4 kg of tissue that controls thought, movement, sensation and every organ.

organs.name: Cerebellum
organs.summary: The 'little brain' behind the brainstem coordinates balance, posture and the timing of movements.

organs.name: Brainstem
organs.summary: Midbrain, pons and medulla connect the brain to the spinal cord and run breathing, heart rate and consciousness.

organs.name: Eye
organs.summary: The eyeball and its parts: cornea, lens, iris, retina and the tissues that protect and move it.

organs.name: Ear
organs.summary: The external ear gathers sound; the middle and inner ear (not modelled here) convert it to nerve signals and sense balance.

organs.name: Nose
organs.summary: Nasal bones and cartilages shape the nose; the conchae inside warm and filter the air.

organs.name: Tongue
organs.summary: A muscular organ for taste, chewing, swallowing and speech.

organs.name: Larynx
organs.summary: The voice box: a cartilage frame with the vocal ligaments, guarding the airway and producing sound.

organs.name: Trachea & bronchial tree
organs.summary: The windpipe and the branching airways that carry air into every segment of the lungs.

organs.name: Lungs
organs.summary: Two spongy organs of gas exchange. This dataset models the lungs through their segmental bronchial trees and pulmonary vessels rather than as solid lobes.

organs.name: Heart
organs.summary: The four-chambered pump that drives blood around the body.

organs.name: Coronary vessels
organs.summary: The arteries and veins that supply and drain the heart muscle itself.

match.regex: coronary|interventricular (branch|vein)|cardiac vein|marginal (branch|vein)|conus (branch|artery)|posterior vein of left ventricle|septal branch|diagonal branch

organs.name: Aorta
organs.summary: The largest artery, carrying blood from the left ventricle to the whole body.

organs.name: Diaphragm
organs.summary: The dome-shaped muscle separating chest from abdomen; the main muscle of breathing.

organs.name: Oesophagus
organs.summary: A muscular tube carrying swallowed food from the pharynx to the stomach.

organs.name: Stomach
organs.summary: A muscular bag that churns food with acid and enzymes before releasing it into the duodenum.

organs.name: Small intestine
organs.summary: Duodenum, jejunum and ileum: about six metres where most digestion and absorption happens.

organs.name: Large intestine
organs.summary: Caecum, appendix, colon and rectum absorb water and form stool.

organs.name: Liver
organs.summary: The body's chemical factory: it processes nutrients, detoxifies blood and makes bile. Modelled as eight hepatovenous segments with the biliary tree.

match.regex: hepatovenous segment|caudate lobe of liver|hepatic duct|biliary tree|duct of caudate lobe

organs.name: Gallbladder & bile ducts
organs.summary: Stores and concentrates bile, releasing it into the duodenum through the cystic and common bile ducts.

organs.name: Pancreas
organs.summary: Makes digestive enzymes and the hormones insulin and glucagon.

organs.name: Spleen
organs.summary: Filters blood, recycles red cells and houses immune cells.

organs.name: Kidneys
organs.summary: Paired filters that clean the blood and regulate fluid and salts.

organs.name: Adrenal glands
organs.summary: Glands on top of each kidney producing cortisol, aldosterone and adrenaline.

organs.name: Urinary bladder & urethra
organs.summary: The bladder stores urine; the urethra carries it out of the body.

organs.name: Ureters
organs.summary: Muscular tubes carrying urine from the kidneys to the bladder.

organs.name: Prostate
organs.summary: A walnut-sized gland below the bladder that adds fluid to semen.

organs.name: Testes & epididymis
organs.summary: The testes produce sperm and testosterone; the epididymis stores maturing sperm.

organs.name: Penis
organs.summary: Erectile bodies (corpora cavernosa and spongiosum) and the glans.

organs.name: Pituitary gland
organs.summary: The master gland at the base of the brain, controlling growth, thyroid, adrenal and reproductive hormones.

organs.name: Thymus
organs.summary: Behind the sternum; trains T lymphocytes in childhood and shrinks with age.

organs.name: Skull
organs.summary: 22 bones forming the cranium that protects the brain and the facial skeleton.

match.regex: frontal bone|parietal bone|temporal bone|occipital bone|sphenoid|ethmoid|zygomatic|maxilla|mandible|nasal bone|lacrimal bone|palatine bone|vomer|nasal concha|hyoid

organs.name: Vertebral column
organs.summary: 33 vertebrae with their discs: the flexible pillar that carries the head and protects the spinal cord.

organs.name: Rib cage
organs.summary: Twelve pairs of ribs, their costal cartilages and the sternum protect the heart and lungs and move with breathing.

organs.name: Bony pelvis
organs.summary: The two hip bones with the sacrum and coccyx transfer body weight to the legs and protect pelvic organs.

organs.name: Shoulder girdle
organs.summary: Clavicle and scapula link each arm to the trunk.

organs.name: Hand skeleton
organs.summary: 27 bones per hand: 8 carpals, 5 metacarpals and 14 phalanges.

organs.name: Foot skeleton
organs.summary: 26 bones per foot: 7 tarsals, 5 metatarsals and 14 phalanges.

organs.name: Knee joint
organs.summary: The largest joint in the body: femur, tibia and patella held by four ligaments and cushioned by two menisci, with the fibula alongside.
